name: Progressive Web App (PWA)
apex: Turns an app into an installable, offline-capable web app: manifest, icons, shortcuts, screenshots, push notifications, service worker hooks, set per-application.
workflow: Enable in Create Application Wizard or Shared Components > Progressive Web App, then set installability/appearance/notification attributes.
relevance: Paddock is already a PWA via serwist configured in code; this is an app-shell admin page, not a page-composition component the designer would offer.
skip_for_web: Application-wide PWA manifest config, not a designer component.

name: Deleting an Application
apex: Removes an application definition and optionally drops its supporting database objects, from the Application home page Tasks list or Edit Application Definition.
workflow: Click Delete this Application (or Delete on Edit Application Definition), confirm Permanently Delete Now.
relevance: Generic app-deletion admin flow; the analogous Paddock Developer concept is Delete Page, already covered elsewhere.
skip_for_web: trivial CRUD confirmation dialog

name: AI page (Generative AI attributes)
apex: Application-level settings enabling an AI Assistant at runtime: pick a default AI Service and optional PL/SQL request/response handler procedures for logging, masking or policy.
workflow: Edit Application Definition > AI tab; select a configured Generative AI Service, optionally wire handler procedures.
relevance: Ties AI features to PL/SQL procedures unique to the Oracle DB runtime; any Paddock AI feature would be a Next.js API route, not a designer attribute.

name: Application Icons
apex: One uploaded icon is auto-resized to five sizes (32-512px) and reused as favicon, PWA icon, Apple touch icon, App Builder icon, sign-in page and home breadcrumb.
workflow: Upload once in User Interface attributes or via Customize > Edit App Icon at runtime; APEX resizes and reuses everywhere.
relevance: The built-in icon-library-plus-color-picker (pick color, then icon) is the right pattern for an Icon attribute inside Cards, not just the favicon use case.

name: Developer Comments
apex: Free-text comments attachable to an application, a page, or a group of pages via a Developer Comment button, with a dedicated list and calendar view.
workflow: Click the word-balloon Developer Comment icon on any app/page screen, type a note, or browse/delete past notes from Shared Components.
relevance: A team-workflow annotation tool (bugs/to-dos) for multi-developer teams; Paddock is a two-person repo already using git commits and HANDOFF.md for this.

name: Find (global Finder)
apex: A single search flyout, opened from a flashlight icon on most App Builder screens, with tabs to search Items, Pages, Queries, Tables, PL/SQL, plus Debug/Session/Errors reports.
workflow: Click the Find icon anywhere, pick a tab, type a case-insensitive query, click Go, click a result to jump to it.
relevance: Directly matches the open Paddock Developer walkthrough item that Page Finder needs search: one global Finder searching pages/components/queries is the pattern to copy.
skip_for_web: the Tables/PL-SQL/Session/Debug tabs are DB-runtime-specific, not applicable

name: Application Comments
apex: A single free-text Comments field on an application (via Shared Components > Edit Application Comment) to describe the app or note who worked on it.
workflow: Shared Components > Edit Application Comment, type text, Apply Changes.
relevance: Trivial metadata field; not a page component or designer capability.

name: Application Groups
apex: Named groups that applications can be assigned to, used only to filter/organize the App Builder home page listing of many separate applications.
workflow: Create a group under Workspace Utilities, then bulk-assign or unassign applications to it from a filterable report.
relevance: Solves organizing many separate apps in one workspace; Paddock Developer is one application with many pages, so Page Groups (not covered here) would be the closer analogue.
skip_for_web: multi-application workspace organization, not page composition

name: Locking and Unlocking an Application
apex: A developer can lock an app for exclusive editing, blocking every other developer from changing it through App Builder until the locker unlocks it.
workflow: From App Builder home (Actions column) or the Application home Tasks list, click the lock icon, add a comment, Lock Application; only that developer can edit or unlock it.
relevance: Paddock Developer is a multi-admin designer (workspace = Clerk Organization); an exclusive edit-lock with a visible status icon prevents two admins clobbering the same page/app.

name: Application Utilities (hub)
apex: A landing page of links to app-level reports and tools (dashboard, advisor, backups, checksums, embedded code, DB dependencies, APEX views, IR utilities) for inspecting one application.
workflow: Application home page > Utilities icon, then pick a link.
relevance: Most links are Oracle-DB-runtime diagnostics (SQL/PLSQL scans, deployment checksums) that have no equivalent in a git-deployed Next.js site; the useful ideas (dashboard, recent pages, change history) are captured as their own notes.
skip_for_web: most sub-tools are DB-specific

name: Application Dashboard
apex: A single overview page charting one application's shape: overview stats, security summary, template usage, counts of pages by page type, and counts of application- and page-level components, plus two utilization charts.
attributes: Pages by Type (DML Form, Dynamic Form, Cards, Faceted Search, Interactive Grid, Interactive Report, Report, Static HTML...)
Application Components (Computations, Items, Processes, Lists, LOVs, Plug-ins, Shortcuts, Tabs)
Page Components (Buttons, Branches, Dynamic Actions, Report Columns, Items, Regions)
workflow: Application home > Utilities > Application Dashboard; click a count to drill into that report.
relevance: Directly matches the planned Health phase: a page listing counts of pages-by-type and component usage across the whole site is exactly the cross-app health/inventory view Paddock Developer needs before PR 4.2 Health.
skip_for_web: the Security/Templates sub-reports are APEX-auth specific

name: Recently Updated Pages report
apex: A simple report listing pages the current user has recently edited, reached from Application Utilities.
workflow: Application home > Utilities > Recently Updated Pages.
relevance: A small, cheap widget worth adding to a designer home/dashboard so an admin can jump back into pages they were just editing.

name: Change History report
apex: An audit-trail report of edits made to the current application, grouped by developer, component type, and page number, filterable by a time window.
workflow: Application home > Utilities > Change History; pick a Since range and click Set.
relevance: With multiple admins editing the same site, a filterable who-changed-what-when log is a useful accountability screen for the designer's admin area.

name: Database Object Dependencies
apex: Scans an application's SQL/PL-SQL for referenced tables, views, columns, packages and procedures, then shows them in a tree plus an error list for broken references.
workflow: Utilities > Database Object Dependencies > Scan Application, choose scan type and scope, browse the resulting tree, click a component link to jump to it.
relevance: Paddock has no scattered raw SQL/PL-SQL inside pages to scan; component-to-component dependency tracking is better covered by the Application Dashboard's component counts.
skip_for_web: literal database-object dependency scanning

name: Accessing Application Utilities
apex: Navigation-only page: select an application then click the Utilities icon to reach the Application Utilities hub.
workflow: App Builder home > select app > Utilities icon.
relevance: Pure navigation step, no new concept beyond the Application Utilities hub already noted.

name: Application Utilities Page (link table)
apex: A reference table describing every link on the Application Utilities page (Dashboard, Advisor, Upgrade, Recently Updated Pages, Attribute Dictionary, Change History, DB dependencies, Debug Messages, APEX Views, Export Repository, Backups, Embedded Code, Page/Cross-Page Utilities, IR Utilities, checksums, Font APEX icons).
workflow: Reference documentation only, no separate workflow.
relevance: Restates the hub's link list already captured; the individually valuable items (Dashboard, Recently Updated, Change History) are noted separately.

name: APEX Views
apex: A metadata query browser exposing data-dictionary views of an application definition, with column picking, a generated SQL query, tree view, and CSV-style download.
workflow: Utilities > Oracle APEX Views, pick a view, choose columns, click Results, optionally download.
relevance: Raw metadata-as-SQL browsing has no equivalent need in a Next.js site where the schema is TypeScript types and Supabase tables, already queryable directly.

name: Application Backups
apex: Automatic daily snapshots of every modified application, last 25 kept, plus on-demand manual backups, each restorable, downloadable, lockable against deletion, or removable, with a per-backup change summary of new, modified and deleted pages and components.
attributes: Restore (Restore Application ID / Auto Assign New ID / Change Application ID)
workflow: Workspace Utilities > Manage Backups, pick an app, then Restore, Download, Lock or Delete a specific dated revision, or click Create Backup for a manual snapshot with comments.
relevance: A revision history with one-click restore and a diff-style change summary is the safety net a live content designer needs beyond git commits, since admins edit rows directly, not through PRs.
skip_for_web: the multi-workspace deployment angle

name: Embedded Code Utility
apex: A single faceted-search page listing every inline SQL, PL-SQL or JavaScript snippet used anywhere in an application, in pages or shared components, for code review, security audit, or tuning without opening every property.
workflow: Utilities > Embedded Code; filter by language, scope and component type; click Download for an offline ZIP of every snippet.
relevance: Matches an existing concern that code-served blocks are hard to govern: a faceted inventory of every custom HTML or script snippet, filterable by page and type, is the audit tool needed before they spread further.

name: Page and Application Checksums
apex: A generated hash identifying an exact app or page definition, including page, region and item counts, used to verify the same version is deployed identically across separate workspaces.
attributes: Page Checksum report (Name, Page, Alias, Checksum, Updated By, Group, Updated)
Checksum window (via Page Designer Utilities menu)
workflow: Utilities > Application Checksum or Page Checksum; copy the hash and compare it to another deployment.
relevance: Paddock verifies deployment identity via git SHA and CI, an exact diff rather than a hash comparison; no gap to fill.
skip_for_web: solves cross-workspace deployment drift, not applicable to a single git-deployed site

name: Font APEX (icon library)
apex: The built-in icon library, over 1150 icons, backing every Icon attribute in APEX: Small (16x16, for buttons and menus) and Large (32x32, for Cards, media lists and hero regions) variants, plus 25 layerable modifiers, with a live-preview picker generating copyable HTML markup.
attributes: Pick Icon dialog (from Appearance Icon on a component)
workflow: Utilities > Font APEX Icons to browse and copy markup, or click the Icon attribute LOV on a component in Page Designer to pick straight from the same library.
relevance: This is the reusable icon-picker Cards Icon and Badge attributes need: one shared library with size variants tied to card template density, not a bespoke uploader per component.
skip_for_web: the animation and rotate flourishes are unlikely to be needed

name: Page Specific Utilities (menu)
apex: A links region on the Utilities page routing to per-page and cross-page tooling: Cross Page Utilities, Page Groups, and Region, Button, Item, Computation, Validation, Process, Dynamic Action and Branch utilities.
workflow: Utilities page > Page Specific Utilities region, click a link.
relevance: Pure navigation menu; the one substantive idea it points to, Page Groups for organizing many pages, is not elaborated in this file.

name: Cross Page Utilities
apex: Reports spanning every page in one application: bulk Delete Multiple Pages, a Page Attributes inventory (name, title, group, type, component and control counts, logic) per page, and Page Locks to stop two developers editing the same page.
workflow: Utilities > Cross Page Utilities, pick a report; from Page Attributes click a page number to open it.
relevance: The Page Attributes inventory, every page with its type and component counts in one searchable table, is a good model for a sitemap and audit screen; Page Locks extends the lock to page granularity.

name: Interactive Report Utilities (admin)
apex: Admin-level governance over end-user report customization: a list of all saved, non-default interactive reports across the app, and a list of report email subscriptions, each bulk-deletable.
attributes: Saved Reports (page, region, report type, name, static ID, owner)
workflow: Utilities > Saved Reports or Subscriptions, filter and select rows, Delete Checked to remove them.
relevance: Foreshadows a real need if the Table component lets users save custom views: an admin screen to audit and clean up other users saved views or subscriptions across the whole site.
skip_for_web: email subscription delivery, unlikely for Paddock data tables

name: Workspace Utilities (hub)
apex: A landing page one level above Application Utilities, linking to workspace-wide tools: REST Enabled SQL Services, Generative AI, Remote Servers, Application Groups, Web Credentials, Export, APEX Views, Manage Backups, REST Source Catalogs, Vector Providers, Cross Application Reports.
workflow: App Builder home > Workspace Utilities icon, then pick a link.
relevance: A workspace holds many separate applications; Paddock Developer administers one site, so most of these multi-app tools have no target.

name: Accessing Workspace Utilities
apex: Navigation-only page: click the Workspace Utilities icon on the App Builder home page.
workflow: App Builder home page > Workspace Utilities icon.
relevance: Pure navigation, no new concept.

name: Workspace Utilities Page (link table)
apex: Reference table describing each Workspace Utilities link, including Team Development (conversational issue tracking with templates, labels, milestones) and OpenTelemetry (collects page load time and interaction data).
workflow: Reference documentation only.
relevance: Restates the hub already noted; OpenTelemetry performance monitoring is interesting in spirit but Paddock already tracks perf baselines separately outside any APEX-style designer screen.

name: Vector Providers
apex: Workspace-level config that turns text into a vector embedding, backed by a database ONNX model, a Generative AI Service, or a custom PL/SQL function, for semantic search or similarity queries.
attributes: Provider Type: Database ONNX Model / Generative AI Service / Custom PL/SQL
AI Provider (OCI, OpenAI, Cohere, Google Gemini, Generic)
workflow: Workspace Utilities > Vector Providers > Create, choose a provider type and its specific attributes, then reference it from an Oracle Vector Search configuration.
relevance: Backend AI/vector-database infrastructure, not a page-composition component; a future semantic search feature for Paddock would be a Next.js API integration, not a designer attribute.

name: Cross Application Reports
apex: Reports spanning every separate application in a workspace: Application Attributes, Build/App Status, Build Options, Developer Comments, Security Profiles, Authentication Schemes, Password Items, Theme Summary.
workflow: Workspace Utilities > Cross Application Reports region > All Reports, pick a report.
relevance: Solves comparing many separate applications in one workspace; Paddock Developer manages a single application with many pages, so there is nothing cross-application to report on.

name: Theme and Library Applications
apex: Special stub applications that hold only shared components, themes, lists, LOVs or workflows, published so other applications can subscribe and get update prompts when the source changes.
workflow: Create a normal app, delete all its pages, set Application Type to Theme (or use Create Library Application), then group shared components for other apps to subscribe to.
relevance: Solves distributing one design system across many separate applications; Paddock Developer is building the component system directly into its one site, not packaging it for external subscribers.
skip_for_web: the subscribe-and-refresh-prompt pattern already exists elsewhere in Paddock Shared Components

name: Creating Theme Applications
apex: Step-by-step: create a blank app, bulk-delete all its pages via Cross Page Utilities, then switch Application Type to Theme in the application definition.
workflow: Create Application, delete all pages, Edit Application Definition > Properties > Application Type = Theme, Apply Changes.
relevance: Same multi-application distribution mechanism as the parent topic, not applicable to a single-site designer.

name: Creating Library Applications
apex: A dedicated Create Library Application wizard entry that produces an app meant to hold only shared components (lists, LOVs, workflows) for other apps to subscribe to.
workflow: App Builder home > Tasks > Create Library Application, name it, then assign shared components into component groups.
relevance: Same multi-application distribution mechanism, not applicable to a single-site designer.

name: Adding a New Page Using Generative AI
apex: A chat-driven Create Page flow: the APEX Assistant asks for a natural-language description of the page and its data, proposes a summary, lets the developer refine it with more messages, then generates the actual page attributes for review before creation.
attributes: Using Generative AI (default Create Page option)
workflow: Create Page, accept Using Generative AI, describe the page and table in plain language, refine with follow-up messages, then review and edit the generated attributes before creating.
relevance: A strong pattern for Paddock Developer: let an admin type "standings table for F1 2026" and get a scaffolded Table/Cards page with the right component and columns pre-picked, still editable before commit.

name: Copying Application Pages
apex: A Copy Page Wizard, reachable from Create Page or the Page Designer Create menu, that duplicates a page, optionally into a different application or user interface/theme, with a choice to copy shared components or remap them to existing ones in the target.
workflow: From Create Page Wizard choose Create Page as Copy, or in Page Designer use Create > Copy Page, then choose the target and how shared components should map.
relevance: Duplicate Page as a first-class action, with an explicit choice to share or fork the underlying List/Component Settings, is a pattern worth copying so templated pages (driver card, race page) do not silently diverge.
skip_for_web: cross-application and cross-theme copying, since Paddock is one site

name: About Deleting Application Pages
apex: Deleting a page also deletes the tabs, breadcrumbs and list entries that pointed to it, and a page can only be deleted if it is unlocked or locked by the current developer.
workflow: Implicit: deleting a page triggers cleanup of dependent navigation entries automatically; a locked-by-someone-else page cannot be deleted.
relevance: Directly answers an open Paddock Developer question: Delete Page must cascade to remove the page from any nav menu, breadcrumb or list that references it, not just remove the page row.

name: Locking and Unlocking a Page
apex: Per-page exclusive edit lock with the same three-state icon as application locks (unlocked/locked-by-me/locked-by-other), settable from the Application home report, the Page Designer toolbar, or a bulk Page Locks utility, with a comment and full lock history; a Workspace Administrator can force-unlock pages other developers locked.
workflow: Lock from the app report view, the Page Designer toolbar, or Cross Page Utilities Page Locks for bulk lock/unlock; only the locker or an admin can unlock.
relevance: Adds the missing pieces for a multi-admin designer: a lock button inline in the page editor itself, bulk lock/unlock across many pages, and an admin override so a forgotten lock never blocks the team.

name: Report Options in the Create Application Wizard
apex: A taxonomy of the six report page types the Create Application Wizard can add: Cards, Faceted Search, Smart Filters, Interactive Grid, Interactive Report, and Classic Report, each with its defining trait.
attributes: Cards: Card Title, Description Column, Additional Text Column
Faceted Search: auto-discovers facets from a Table, not from a View
Smart Filters: single search field plus suggestion chips with occurrence counts, more space-efficient than Faceted Search
Interactive Grid: Allow Editing or Read Only, mouse/keyboard rearrangeable
Interactive Report: optional Include Form, Lookup Columns for foreign keys
Classic Report: optional Include Form, Lookup Columns
workflow: Create Application Wizard > Add Page > pick a report type; each type asks for a table/view/query first, then type-specific display columns.
relevance: This is the exact taxonomy to decide against: whether Table, Cards and Filters are three independent components or, like Faceted Search and Smart Filters, thin filter layers in front of a Table or Cards display.

name: Report Options in the Create Page Wizard
apex: Same six report types as the app wizard, added to an existing app: Faceted Search and Smart Filters let the developer pick classic report or cards report as the display, and foreign-key columns auto-map to a Select List via a shared LOV.
attributes: choose underlying render: classic report vs cards report (Faceted Search, Smart Filters)
BLOB columns auto-excluded (Interactive Grid) or set to Download BLOB type (Interactive Report, Classic Report)
foreign key columns auto-mapped to Select List / Plain Text via a Shared LOV (created or reused)
Editing Enabled toggle spawns a separate form page when off
workflow: Create Page > Component > pick a report type > pick Data Source and Source Type > the wizard infers column treatment from constraints automatically.
relevance: Confirms Filters is an orthogonal layer sitting in front of either a Table or Cards display, not a third sibling component; also validates auto-detecting foreign keys into a shared lookup for Table/Cards columns.
skip_for_web: REST Enabled SQL / Duality View / JSON Source source types, no Paddock equivalent

name: Example Cards Page
apex: A worked Cards page on EBA_PROJECTS: Title maps to NAME, Icon maps to PROJECT_LEAD (rendered as icon initials), Body maps to DESCRIPTION, arranged as individual index-card boxes.
attributes: Actions: Button, Full Card, Title, Subtitle, Media
advanced HTML expressions / template directives for conditional formatting
workflow: Pick a table, choose a layout, map Title/Body/Icon Initials/Badge columns; add Actions so the card, title, subtitle or media is clickable; use template directives for conditional styling.
relevance: The Actions model, five distinct clickable zones (Button, Full Card, Title, Subtitle, Media) rather than one generic onClick, is the concrete attribute set the Cards component should copy verbatim.

name: Creating a Cards Page (Create Application Wizard)
apex: Cards-page setup inside the Create Application Wizard: pick a table/view, a layout, and which columns feed Title, Body, Icon Initials and Badge, with Title and Body pre-selected automatically from the Data Dictionary Cache.
workflow: Add Page > Cards > pick table, layout and the four content columns (Title/Body pre-guessed), optionally mark it Home or Administration page.
relevance: Smart-guessing Title and Body columns from the data dictionary before the developer chooses is a good default-generation trick worth copying in a Paddock create-page flow.
skip_for_web: Set as Administration Page, no admin/end-user split needed in Paddock pages

name: Creating a Cards Page (Create Page Wizard)
apex: Adding a Cards page to an existing app: choose a Data Source (Local Database, REST Enabled SQL, REST Source, Duality View, JSON Source, or Sample Data) and Source Type, set Navigation options, then the same Layout and card content columns as the app wizard.
attributes: Source Type: Table/View or SQL Query
workflow: Create Page, Cards, choose data source and source type, toggle breadcrumb/nav auto-entry named after the page, pick layout and card columns, then Create Page.
relevance: The Use Breadcrumb / Use Navigation toggles, defaulted on and named after the page, show that every new-page wizard should offer to auto-wire navigation instead of leaving it a separate manual step.
skip_for_web: REST Enabled SQL / Duality View / JSON Source data sources

name: Example Smart Filters (interaction model)
apex: A worked Smart Filters page on EMP: a single search field with filter suggestion chips beneath it, each chip showing how often that value occurs; clicking a chip name opens its value list, clicking elsewhere quick-applies it and moves it to an Applied Filters area.
attributes: click name to browse values vs click chip body to quick-apply
X to remove an applied filter
re-open an applied chip to change its value
workflow: Click a chip name to see its values, click the rest of the chip to quick-apply a value, remove it via the X on an applied chip.
relevance: The two-click-targets-per-chip trick, browse vs instant-apply, packs full faceted filtering into one compact row instead of a sidebar; this is a strong candidate for Paddock Filters on dense standings and results tables.

name: Auto-Discovered Filters and the Data Dictionary Cache
apex: When a Smart Filters (or Faceted Search) page is built on a real table, the wizard auto-selects which columns become filters using a statistics-driven relevance score from the Data Dictionary Cache, not developer guesswork; building on a view or query falls back to VARCHAR2 columns.
attributes: Table Column Cache report (preview of scoring)
top five facet search score columns with score >= 20
Gather Statistics and Refresh Cache / Refresh Cache Only
workflow: Build the page on a table; the wizard silently profiles column statistics and pre-picks the best five filterable columns, which the developer can still override.
relevance: A concrete, scriptable idea: profile a Postgres/Supabase table's own column stats to auto-suggest which columns make good Filters facets, instead of asking the admin to guess every time.

name: Search Filter Types
apex: The set of facet input types a Smart Filters region supports, each with distinct storage and comparison behavior, configured per filter via Identification > Type in Page Designer.
attributes: Checkbox Group (multi-select from an LOV, stored colon-delimited)
Input Field (free text, developer- or user-chosen comparison operator, date/timestamp canonical format)
Range (LOV of ranges, lower bound inclusive/upper bound exclusive, syntax like |100, 100|500, 500|, supports manual entry)
Search (one per region, always pinned to the top regardless of sequence)
workflow: Select a filter in the Rendering tree, set Identification > Type, then configure the type-specific attributes (LOV, comparison operator, range boundaries).
relevance: This is the exact facet-type taxonomy Paddock Filters should offer: checkbox/radio for team or category, range for lap times or points with proper inclusive/exclusive boundaries, and one pinned free-text search box.

name: Creating Smart Filters (Create Application Wizard)
apex: Wizard flow to add a Smart Filters page: choose the underlying display (Report or Cards), pick a table, and, only when the underlying display is a classic Report, optionally auto-generate a linked create and update form page.
workflow: Add Page > Smart Filters > choose Report or Cards, pick a table, optionally enable Include Form for a Report.
relevance: Confirms Filters is a thin layer fronting either a Table or Cards display, and that auto-generating a paired edit form is only offered at whole-app creation time, worth deciding deliberately for Paddock.
skip_for_web: the Include Form auto-generated edit form, since Paddock content pages are typically read-only

name: Creating Smart Filters (Create Page Wizard)
apex: Same Data Source and Navigation setup as other Create Page Wizard reports, then a Display As choice (Report or Cards) and a Select filters step where recommended filters come from table column statistics, refreshable on demand.
workflow: Create Page > Smart Filters > pick data source/source type > Display As > review recommended filters and click Refresh if the data has changed, then Create Page.
relevance: Exposing a manual Refresh on the auto-suggested filter list, rather than only computing it once, is the detail that makes stats-based facet suggestion trustworthy for a live-editing admin.

name: Smart Filters as a decoupled region
apex: Built manually, a Smart Filters region is its own region (Identification Type = Smart Filters) that references an existing classic report, cards, map or calendar region by name via Source > Filtered Region, rather than being baked into that region.
attributes: Source, Database Column(s) on the search item (comma list for multi-column search)
supported targets: classic report, cards, map, calendar
workflow: Create the target report/cards/map/calendar region first, then add a separate Smart Filters region and point its Filtered Region at it; bind the built-in search item to several columns at once.
relevance: Confirms Filters should be built as an independent component that attaches to any compatible display region by reference, not fused into Table or Cards, and that its search box can span multiple columns at once.
skip_for_web: map and calendar targets, no Paddock equivalent yet

name: Filter List of Values sourcing and Range static values
apex: Each filter picks its own value source: Shared Component (reuse a named LOV resolving a foreign key to a display label), Distinct Values (auto-derive uniques from the column), or Static Values (developer-typed display/return pairs) to hand-build Range buckets.
attributes: List of Values, Type: Shared Component / Distinct Values / Static Values
Static Values editor (Display Value / Return Value rows)
workflow: On a filter, set List of Values Type; for Range with hand-picked buckets use Static Values and enter Display/Return pairs with the lower-inclusive, upper-exclusive pipe syntax.
relevance: Three independent LOV strategies per filter, reuse a lookup, auto-distinct, or hand-authored buckets, is exactly the flexibility Paddock Filters needs for things like lap-time or points ranges versus team-name checkboxes.

name: Filters as a distinct entity type
apex: A filter is not a page item even when it shares a type name like Checkbox Group: it is tied to one column of the Filtered Region, named P<page>_<name> by convention, ordered by dragging, and mostly unreachable by dynamic actions built for items.
attributes: creatable types: Checkbox Group, Input Field, Radio Group, Range
exactly one Search-type filter always present, not separately creatable
workflow: Right-click the Filters node under a Smart Filters region, Create Filter, pick a type, bind it to a column, then drag to set its display order.
relevance: Confirms Paddock Filters should be its own component model bound to a column, not a repurposed form input, with a fixed single search slot plus an orderable list of typed facets.

name: Suggestions (chip preview value)
apex: A collapsed filter chip shows one candidate value plus its count before the user opens the list; which value it previews is configured separately from the full List of Values, as Dynamic (first visible LOV entry), Static Values (a fixed comma list), or SQL Query.
attributes: Suggestions, Static Values setting: Dynamic / Static Values / SQL Query
workflow: On a filter, set Suggestions to control what shows on its collapsed chip, independent of the full value list it opens to.
relevance: A non-obvious but important detail: the compact chip preview needs its own small config separate from the facet full value list, otherwise a high-cardinality facet chip has nothing sensible to show before it is opened.

name: LOV size guardrail
apex: A hard cap on how many distinct values a filter list of values or Distinct Values source may return: 5000 maximum, with a runtime error raised once more than 2000 items come back, since that is unusable as a search UI.
workflow: Implicit: APEX enforces this automatically when rendering a filter list of values.
relevance: A concrete guardrail Paddock Filters should copy: cap or paginate a facet high-cardinality value list and fail loudly rather than render thousands of checkboxes.

name: Client-Side Filtering on a facet value list
apex: An attribute that adds a live type-to-narrow search box above a single facet own value list, letting a user search within a large set of options, for example typing develop to narrow a Project list.
workflow: Enable Client-Side Filtering on a filter; opening its chip now shows a small search field above the option list.
relevance: Search-the-facet-itself is exactly what a Driver, Circuit or Team filter with many options needs on Paddock tables, rather than forcing a long scroll through checkboxes.

name: Depending On (cascading filters)
apex: An attribute that hides a filter chip until another named filter has a value selected, then narrows its own value list to options valid for that selection, for example a Milestone filter that only appears, with relevant milestones, after a Project is chosen.
workflow: On the dependent filter, set Depending On > Filter to the controlling filter name; its chip stays hidden and its list stays empty until the controlling filter has a value.
relevance: Cascading facets are a must-have for Paddock, for example narrowing a Driver filter by a chosen Team, or a Race filter by a chosen Season, exactly this hide-until-parent-selected behavior.

name: Example Faceted Search (layout and facet charts)
apex: A faceted search page puts a facet Search region on the left and a Search Results report or cards region on the right; any facet configured to compute counts automatically gets a chart view of its value distribution.
attributes: left Search region / right Search Results split layout
click a pie slice to drill into it
workflow: Select facet values on the left to narrow the report; open a facet three-dot menu and choose Show Chart for a bar or pie chart, click a slice for detail.
relevance: An interactive count chart hanging off any facet, bar or pie, drillable into a slice, is a distinctive feature worth adding to Paddock Filters, for example a live points-by-team pie chart on a standings filter.
skip_for_web: the left-sidebar layout itself, since Smart Filters compact chips already cover the same ground more efficiently

name: Creating Faceted Search (Create Application Wizard)
apex: Wizard flow identical in shape to Smart Filters: choose Report or Cards as the underlying display, pick a table, and Include Form is offered only for a Report and only from this whole-app wizard.
attributes: Include Form (Report only, app wizard only)
workflow: Add Page > Faceted Search > choose Report or Cards, pick a table, optionally Include Form.
relevance: Repeats the same wizard mechanics already captured under Smart Filters, confirming APEX treats the two as siblings, nothing new for the designer plan.

name: Creating Faceted Search (Create Page Wizard)
apex: Same Data Source, Source Type and Navigation setup as other Create Page Wizard reports; facet columns can be hand-picked for any data source, with statistics-based recommendations and a Refresh button when the source is a local table.
attributes: facet selection (manual for any source, recommended for local tables)
workflow: Create Page > Faceted Search > data source/source type > Display As > review or hand-pick facet columns > Create Page.
relevance: Repeats the statistics-based recommendation and Refresh pattern already captured under Smart Filters; no new mechanic for the designer plan.

name: Example Interactive Grid
apex: A spreadsheet-like report where end users can lock, hide, filter, freeze, highlight and sort columns, add control breaks and aggregations, and save the result as a private or public report; editable grids add a Row Actions menu plus Edit, Save and Add Row buttons.
workflow: Open the Actions or a column heading menu to freeze, hide, sort, highlight or break on a column; drag column headers to reorder; save the customized layout as a report.
relevance: Freeze, highlight and control-break-with-aggregation are genuinely useful power-user features for a long standings or results table, worth offering as opt-in Table capabilities even on a mostly read-only site.
skip_for_web: the fully editable add/save/delete-row mode, since Paddock public tables are read-only

name: Supported Columns in Interactive Grids
apex: The full list of built-in column display/input types an Interactive Grid column can be set to via Identification > Type, spanning simple display types through rich form-input types.
workflow: Select a column in Page Designer, set Identification > Type to change how that column displays or accepts input.
relevance: Only the display-oriented subset matters here: Percent Graph for gap-to-leader bars, HTML Expression for colored team chips, Link to a driver page, plus Row Actions Menu and Row Selector for admin edit screens.
skip_for_web: Color Picker, Password, Rich Text Editor, Markdown Editor, Shuttle, Switch, Star Rating: form-input types with no public-table use case

name: Creating an Interactive Grid (Create Application Wizard)
apex: Wizard flow for a new app containing an Interactive Grid page: pick a Page Source (Table/View or SQL Query), then explicitly choose Allow Editing or Read Only for the whole grid.
attributes: Page Source: Table or View / SQL Query
workflow: Add Page > Interactive Grid > pick the source, choose Allow Editing or Read Only, Add Page.
relevance: A simple binary editable-or-read-only switch at creation time is a good minimal control for a Table component meant to serve both public read-only pages and an admin data-entry screen from the same base.
skip_for_web: Set as Administration Page

name: Creating an Interactive Grid (Create Page Wizard)
apex: Adding an Interactive Grid to an existing app, with an Include Form Page flag that auto-generates a paired edit form as a Modal Dialog page rather than a separate full navigation page.
workflow: Create Page > Interactive Grid > optionally enable Include Form Page for an auto-generated modal edit form, pick data source and source type, set navigation, Create Page.
relevance: Pairing a grid with an auto-generated modal edit form, instead of navigating to a whole new page, is a good default for Paddock admin editing of table rows like race results or driver bios.
skip_for_web: REST/Duality/JSON data sources

name: Master Detail from an Existing Interactive Grid
apex: Two editable Interactive Grids stacked on one page, wired declaratively: the child Master Region attribute points at the parent region, and its Master Column, the child foreign-key column, filters child rows to the selected parent row, no code required.
workflow: Create the parent grid, add a child grid with Create Region Below, set its Source, then set Master Region and Master Column to link it to the parent.
relevance: A declarative parent-child Table link, for example Season to Races or Team to Drivers on one page, each row click auto-filtering the child table, is a strong Table component capability worth adopting.
skip_for_web: the editable add/update/delete-row mechanics

name: Managing Interactive Grid Attributes (hub)
apex: Table-of-contents page linking to the specific Interactive Grid attribute topics: editing attributes, making it editable, pagination, toolbar, saving public reports, flashback and charts, download formats, icon view, detail view.
workflow: Navigation only.
relevance: Pure hub, each linked topic is captured in its own note.

name: Editing Interactive Grid Attributes (Property Editor navigation)
apex: Generic steps to reach an Interactive Grid own attributes in Page Designer, with a Filter Properties search box and a Go to Group jump list for finding one attribute among many grouped ones.
workflow: Select the grid region, open the Attributes tab, type in Filter Properties or use Go to Group to jump straight to a setting.
relevance: A searchable, grouped property panel is the right pattern for Paddock Table/Cards/Filters components too, since each will accumulate many grouped settings over time.

name: Making an Existing Interactive Grid Editable
apex: The Edit attribute group that turns a read-only grid into a data-entry surface: which operations are allowed, an optional column flagging row-by-row whether a row may change, how concurrent edits are protected, and whether an empty result still shows one blank row.
attributes: Allowed Operations: Add Row/Update Row/Delete Row
Lost Update Type: Row Values (checksum) / Row Version Column
workflow: Turn Enabled On (auto-creates the save process), pick Allowed Operations, optionally point Allowed Row Operations Column at a column that vetoes edit/delete per row, and choose a Lost Update Type.
relevance: Allowed Row Operations Column, letting data say which rows are locked from editing, for example a published race result, is useful for an admin edit grid; the checksum-based Lost Update Type is ready-made optimistic concurrency.
skip_for_web: most of this only matters once Paddock has an editable admin data grid, not for public pages

name: Controlling Interactive Grid Pagination
apex: Two pagination models, Page (classic row-set paging with forward/back controls, page size chosen via the Actions menu) or Scroll (rows fill the visible height and more load as the user scrolls), plus an optional total row count in the footer.
workflow: On the grid Attributes, set Pagination Type to Page or Scroll, and decide whether to show a total count.
relevance: Show Total Row Count needs an extra query and can hurt performance on large data sets: a results Table with a total count on a big season table should make that an explicit, opt-in cost.

name: Customizing the Interactive Grid Toolbar
apex: Per-grid control over which built-in toolbar controls appear, or hiding the toolbar entirely.
attributes: Search Column Selection (restrict search to one column)
Reset Button (discard all customizations, reload report definition from the server)
workflow: On the grid Attributes, open the Toolbar group, toggle Show and each Controls checkbox, and rename the Add button label if desired.
relevance: This exact toggle set, search-one-column, actions menu, reset-to-server-defaults, save, custom add-button label, is the right shape for a configurable Table toolbar in Paddock Developer.

name: Enabling Users to Save Public Reports
apex: A toggle that lets authenticated end users save their current grid customization as a Public report visible to everyone in the toolbar report list, gated by an optional authorization scheme; only the report creator may later save, rename or delete it.
workflow: Turn Save Public Report On, optionally restrict it to an authorization scheme; any qualifying user can then save the current filter/column state as a shared named view.
relevance: The ownership rule, anyone can use a shared saved view but only its creator can edit or delete it, is the model Paddock Table saved views should copy if users can save custom filter sets.

name: Enabling Flashback and Charts
apex: Two independent end-user capabilities: Flashback lets a user query the grid as it looked at a past point in time using Oracle point-in-time recovery, and Define Chart View lets a user build their own ad hoc chart directly from the grid data at runtime.
workflow: Toggle Flashback or Define Chart View On in the Enable Users To group; end users then get a time-travel query option or a self-service chart builder on the grid toolbar.
relevance: A self-service, end-user-built chart on top of any table is a strong feature idea for Paddock standings and results tables; the Flashback time-travel query has no Postgres/Supabase equivalent worth building.
skip_for_web: Flashback, an Oracle-specific point-in-time query feature

name: Configuring Interactive Grid Download Formats
apex: Per-grid control over whether and how end users export data: an on/off switch, an authorization scheme gate, a checklist of formats, optional email delivery, CSV delimiter customization, filename, and a warning banner of supplemental text.
attributes: Send as Email (HTML attachment, needs SMTP)
workflow: Turn Download On, pick an authorization scheme if needed, check the formats to offer, and optionally set filename, CSV delimiters, or a supplemental warning banner.
relevance: This exact format list, CSV/HTML/PDF/Excel plus a named-file and CSV-delimiter override, is the right shape for a Table export feature; the explicit warning that Supplemental Text corrupts CSV is a concrete gotcha worth remembering.
skip_for_web: Send as Email, unlikely to be needed for Paddock public tables

name: Icon View and Detail View: one region, three presentations
apex: A single Interactive Grid region can offer Grid, Icon and Detail as switchable presentations of the same query, toggled by the end user with a view-selector button group, rather than needing separate regions or pages per layout.
attributes: Icon View, Show / Custom / Icon Type (Icon CSS Classes or Image in URL) / Icon / Link Target / Label Column
Detail View, Show / Before Rows / For Each Row / After Rows
workflow: On the grid Attributes, enable Icon View and map an icon/link/label column, or enable Detail View and author a per-row HTML template; users switch views with one click.
relevance: A genuine finding: instead of Table and Cards as separate components, model them as view-modes of one data region so a query flips between table rows, icon tiles and a card-like detail template.

name: Detail View HTML row template
apex: Detail View renders each row from developer-authored HTML wrapped Before Rows and After Rows, with a per-row For Each Row template using column substitution strings for values, labels, row id and row index.
workflow: Write an HTML snippet with substitution tokens for the row template; APEX repeats it once per row between the Before/After wrapper HTML.
relevance: A simple token-substitution row template, rather than a full component builder, is a lightweight way Paddock Cards or a compact list view could let an admin hand-author row markup without a plugin system.

name: Customizing Interactive Grids as an End User (overview)
apex: Summary confirming end users can reorder/sort/filter columns and use the Actions menu to change display, edit data when enabled, and save customizations, with available save options varying by user type.
workflow: Restates capabilities already documented individually.
relevance: Pure summary of attributes already captured in their own notes (toolbar, editability, saved reports).

name: Saving Interactive Grid Reports (report kinds)
apex: A four-tier saved-view ownership model: Private (creator-only), Public (everyone can view, only the creator edits or deletes it, others Save As their own copy), Primary (the developer-set default for all users, cannot be deleted), and Alternative (developer-authored extra layouts, optionally authorization-gated).
workflow: Customize the grid, then Actions > Report > Save As, choose a Type (Private/Public/Alternative) and Name; developers additionally can Save over the Primary report directly.
relevance: This four-tier model, personal view, shared view someone owns, the shipped default, and curated alternates, is the answer for a Paddock Table saved-views feature: default view plus a few admin-curated alternates plus optional personal views.

name: Saving reports: prerequisites and public-report tip
apex: Save and Save As only appear if the application has an authentication scheme and the grid toolbar is enabled; Public report support is off by default; Oracle advises shrinking every column to its smallest reasonable width before saving a shared Public or Primary default.
attributes: application-level authentication scheme required for Save
Toolbar must be enabled for Actions menu to exist
Save Public Report must be explicitly enabled
column Stretch width tip before saving a shared default
workflow: Confirm auth and toolbar are on and Save Public Report is enabled, narrow columns to a sensible width, then save the report as the new shared default.
relevance: The narrow-your-columns-before-sharing tip is a small but real lesson: a saved default view width should be tuned for the common viewer, not left at whatever the last editor happened to have.
skip_for_web: the anonymous-app auth restriction, since Paddock pages mostly do not require login to view

name: Linking to Interactive Grid Reports (URL filter syntax)
apex: A URL syntax lets a link open a specific saved report and/or apply a filter directly, using IG[region]_<report id> to pick a report and IG[region]<operator>_<column>:<value> to set a filter, with a defined operator vocabulary and a ROWFILTER pseudo-column for full-row text search.
attributes: operators: C (Contains), EQ (Equals, default), GTE, GT, LT, LTE, N (Null), NC (Not Contains), NEQ, NN (Not Null), IN, NIN (backslash-escaped comma list)
ROWFILTER (Row Text Contains across all string/number columns)
workflow: Build an f?p= URL with a Request of IG[region]_reportid and/or an item name/value pair using the operator syntax to pre-filter the grid when the link is opened.
relevance: This exact operator vocabulary, contains/equals/gte/lt/in/not-in plus a full-row text search, is a solid reference list for designing Paddock Filters URL query-param contract, and a full-row ROWFILTER is a nice single-param full-text option worth copying.
skip_for_web: the f?p= page-and-session URL mechanics themselves, unique to APEX routing

name: Shareable links to saved reports via Static ID
apex: A saved report own Static ID can be edited to a memorable value, and the Property Editor shows a read-only, copyable Link Example URL that opens that exact saved report from anywhere in the application.
workflow: Select a saved report under the region Saved Reports node, unlock and rename its Static ID, then copy the generated Link Example URL to link to it directly.
relevance: Giving every saved Table view a stable slug and a one-click copyable link is exactly what Paddock needs to make a saved filter set or view genuinely shareable and bookmarkable.

name: Example Interactive Report
apex: A formatted SQL query result with the same end-user customization vocabulary as Interactive Grid (search bar, Actions menu, column menus, hide/filter/highlight/sort, breaks, aggregations, charts, group by, computations, save private/public), but read-oriented, desktop-only, and without grid-style drag rearrange or inline editing.
attributes: per-instance capability restriction (e.g. disable Download or column hiding)
workflow: Build on a table or SQL query; end users customize display via the Actions menu; developers can strip capabilities per report while every report keeps the same menu shape.
relevance: Interactive Report is a lighter, non-editable sibling of Interactive Grid: Paddock only needs one Table component with an editable flag, not two engines; every table should keep the same menu shape when actions are stripped.
skip_for_web: Desktop-only restriction, not applicable since Paddock is responsive by default

name: Supported Columns: Built-in Components
apex: The basic Interactive Report column render types: Display Image, Download BLOB, Hidden, Link, Percent Graph, Plain Text, Plain Text (List of Values), Remove HTML, Rich Text, and Row Selector.
attributes: Plain Text (based on List of Values)
workflow: Set a column Identification > Type to change how its value renders.
relevance: Largely the same display-oriented set already noted for Interactive Grid; Percent Graph, Link, Rich Text and Plain Text via LOV are the ones a Paddock Table column type list should include.
skip_for_web: Download BLOB, Row Selector selection UI not needed for public read-only pages

name: Supported Columns: Theme Components (card fragments inside a report)
apex: A second column-type category, built from Universal Theme template component plug-ins, that renders one or many report rows as card-like fragments without leaving the Report region: Avatar, Badge, Comments, Content Row (title, description and more), Media List, and Timeline.
attributes: available as a single-row partial template or for the whole multi-row report
workflow: Set a column Type to a Theme Component such as Content Row or Media List to render that report rows in a pre-built card-like layout, composed from other columns.
relevance: A major finding: APEX does not force a Table-versus-Cards split, a plain Report can render card-like rows via column types alone, arguing Cards should be Table plus composite row-renderer column types, not a separate surface.

name: Additional Pages: Multiple Reports (bulk scaffolding)
apex: A Create Application Wizard option that scaffolds several Interactive-Report-with-Form page pairs in one pass, one per selected table, letting the developer Edit any of them beforehand to swap in a custom SQL query or a different report type such as Classic Report.
attributes: per-page Edit (custom SQL Query, change report type)
workflow: In the Create Application Wizard, pick several tables under Multiple Reports; the wizard queues one report-with-form page per table, each still editable before creation.
relevance: A bulk create-pages-from-these-N-tables step, each pre-scaffolded but still overridable, is a genuinely useful shortcut for Paddock Developer when standing up several similar pages, such as standings, results and schedule, in one operation.
